newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-POSSIBLE SUCCESSORS TO KEEGAN AT NEWCASTLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-POSSIBLE SUCCESSORS TO KEEGAN AT NEWCASTLE.

text.p: The following is a look at the potential successors to Kevin Keegan, who resigned as manager of English premier league Newcastle United on Wednesday:

Age 45. Hugely successful as a player at Glasgow Celtic and Liverpool and then as manager at Liverpool. Took the Merseysiders to three league championships before resigning suddenly. Took over at Blackburn and, fuelled by the money of businessman Jack Walker led them out of the first division to the English league title in 1995. Now back in his native Scotland working for Glasgow Rangers as a super-scout. On the downside, Dalglish left both Liverpool and Blackburn because of stress, the deciding factor in Keegan's departure from St James's Park. Close friends of the terse Scot say he would be happier alone on the golf course than in the Newcastle cauldron.

Age 47. Former Liverpool and Wales forward who played alongside Keegan at Anfield in the 1970s. As a manager took Swansea from division four to division one in successive seasons. Then moved to Spain to manage Real Sociedad and Real Madrid. His experience at the Bernabeu stadium would stand him in good stead at Newcastle where expectations are similarly gigantic. Has had a tough time as manager at Deportivo La Coruna and announced last week he would leave at the end of this season. His lack of recent silverware and his long absence from the English game may deter Newcastle.

Age 45. Keegan's right-hand man over the past five eventful seasons at Newcastle. Has been associated with Keegan since the 1970s when they played together at Liverpool. They joined Newcastle together as players in 1982 and he returned to the club with Keegan 10 years later. Has never managed before but is popular with the squad and fans. The Magpies may be tempted to keep McDermott for the sake of continuity but he has no track-record in charge of a club and would be a risky choice.

Age 64. Massively successful at Ipswich Town in the late 1970s and early 1980s, guiding the modest east coast side to the F.A. Cup, the UEFA Cup and twice to within a whisker of the English league title. Took England to the semifinals of the 1990 World Cup before joining PSV Eindhoven and then Porto, finding success at both clubs. In his first season at Barcelona, he has struggled to win over the fans. Undoubtedly has the pedigree to take over from Keegan but age is against him. Could be seen as a stop-gap manager to nurture a younger man like Peter Beardsley or Chris Waddle into the role.

Age 43. Newcastle fan from the North East who has had success with every club he has managed. An intelligent manager who brought Darlington back into the Football League, took Leicester into the premier league and has turned current club Aston Villa into title contenders. Little and Villa have both emphatically insisted he is staying put but Newcastle are perhaps the only club who could tempt him away -- and afford to pay Villa the compensation.

Age 35. A Newcastle man through and through, he is coming to the end of his career at the club he supported as a boy. Has said recently he would like to stay on at St James's Park once his playing days are over. Has no experience of managership though, and the club may view him as a good bet for the future rather than the present.

Age 36. Another Geordie who has played for Newcastle and England. Also has continental experience at Marseilles, a qualification seen as ever more important in English soccer. Has expressed an interest in management but, like Beardsley, has no experience of it.
